workflow_hints: Affinity purification coupled with mass spectrometry proteomics

Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The study employs two distinct proteomics workflows: 1) A chemical proteomics approach using drug affinity chromatography (AP-MS) with label-free quantification (spectral counting). 2) A phosphoproteomics approach using both SILAC (for global pS/pT/pY) and label-free (for pY) quantification. Both used DDA acquisition.

organism: Mascot searches were performed against the UniProt human database
noncellular_sources: patient samples were lyzed and total cell lysate containing 5 mg of protein were added to the affinity matrix
scope: c-ceritinib or ampicillin was immobilized on NHS-activated Sepharose for Fast Flow resin (GE Healthcare) and blocked with ethanolamine overnight. H650, H23, H3122 cells and patient samples were lyzed and total cell lysate containing 5 mg of protein were added to the affinity matrix for 2 hours.
Tyrosine phoshopeptides were enriched using the PTMScan Phospho-Tyrosine Mouse mAb (P-Tyr-100) Kit
global phosphopeptide enrichment was done using PHOS-Select Iron Affinity Gel (Sigma)

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The experiment utilized two main proteomics approaches: chemical proteomics (affinity purification using c-ceritinib probe) and phosphoproteomics (enrichment of pY and pSTY peptides). Both involve the isolation of a subproteome/complex rather than analysis of whole cell lysate.
